content: They have made it impossible to win level 31 without paying money. after the start of the game, there are 65 cards faced down in the deck, and 30 additional cards face down in the play stacks. Since each card reveal and moving each the card counts as TWO movements, that means if the game is played absolutely perfectly, you need at least 190 moves just to reveal the hidden cards and move them in the right stack. You then need at least an additional 5 moves to move those stacked into the top. That means you need at least 195 moves. The game only gives you 190 moves. content:

It becomes frustrating because it feels less like the outcome depends on skill and more like the game is designed to force you into situations where you either have to buy credits, make in app purchases, or keep losing until the game finally gives you a playable setup.
I don’t mind a game becoming more challenging as you progress, but there’s a difference between increasing the difficulty and making a level practically impossible without spending money. What starts out as a fun game quickly starts feeling like a pay-to-win setup, which takes a lot of the enjoyment out of it.

Then I remembered reading someone else’s review who commented on this same exact issue and an app developer responded. They said that every hand can be won but some are harder than others blah blah blah. I don’t think so! I’ve put in more time on this one level than any sane person should. Plus, getting stuck for weeks on one level just takes the fun out of playing in the first place. I really like the concept though. The harder the better! I don’t mind repeating the level until I can beat it but if I get to the point where I know every card in the deck and still can’t get a winnable hand, something is fishy. An ad before each level? Sure, that’s understandable. An ad if I want extra moves or a boost? Absolutely understandable. Having to watch an ad to return to the main menu? I’ve played the game enough to reach level 244 because I do enjoy the game, but I’m about to delete the app and be done with it because I’m over the ads (particularly the Kalshi adds that are annoying as heck and way, way too long). My second gripe is that many of the words and/or associations are way too obscure and are sometimes inaccurate, which makes it impossible to know where some words belong until you’ve gone through the level 5+ times and finally managed to get a base card uncovered that makes them almost make sense. I understand that’s part of the challenge, but since I have to sit through 30,000 ads per game and between games, it just adds to the annoyance. Developers should consider removing (or at least greatly reducing) within-level ads to make this game more enjoyable. I know me deleting the app is no sweat off your back, but I can guarantee that your excessive ads are driving more people than just me away, so you might want to rethink your strategy.

author: Lola22💛
title: anxious girl approved
content:
okay, i did pay the one-time fee to get rid of the ads in-game. 

however….

it was SO worth it. i play this game for literally hours on end. i’m over level 5,300 lol! 

i’m an anxious person, and being able to turn my brain off and sort things into little piles helps me sort my own brain into piles. 

it’s also fun to see the little bits of “human” popping through. small spelling errors, cute animated drawings, etc. some call it a flaw, or a bug. i call it personality. 

i do think the accuracy of where you put your finger to pick up the card can be bettered, it feels awkward and not properly calibrated. it’s not a massive problem, and doesn’t inhibit gameplay.

another suggestion i have is regarding the weekly challenges and games. 

if the same game repeats each week, like the puzzle pieces, then there should be a way to skip or turn off the instructions each week. the animations are cute, but i dont need to re-read the instructions every week. 

in the same category, the animations after each level of the rewards you earn is played. there should be a way to skip these animations, similarly to a “skip intro” button on a show- or even a way to turn them off entirely. 

but, for a game that just turned a year old, they’re doing SO well.

anyways, yes the one-time fee is annoying and feels kitschy, but if you intend on playing it more than once a week, it’s worth it.

author: Sheigirl
title: Designed to make you pay
content: I usually don’t bother writing reviews for games, but I wanted to make some suggestions so hopefully someone reads this (not that they’ll actually do anything about it). I’ve been playing this game, on and off, for some time now - probably a few years! I will play it for a week or two and then give up on it and then come back to it. When I first started playing, the game was fairly straightforward… like regular solitaire but you had to sort the words under headings. I actually would look up words once in a while to try to expand my vocabulary. My only complaint was that way too often the “randomness” of the cards meant you’d have to restart levels repeatedly or use up your ‘watch an ad for 10 extra moves (sometimes repeatedly) to complete the puzzle. Then they added in locks and keys adding an unnecessary level of difficulty -as far as I can tell, it’s a simple ploy to get more money from players. Now, it’s even harder to complete the puzzles as you pretty much have to play the entire level repeatedly multiple times (thus having to watch multiple ads), or use up most of your “watch an ad for 10 free moves,’ or flat out spend real money to buy more moves. Now, lately, I’ve noticed that even on the easier boards, the game seems to have changed so that you are consistently 1-4 moves away from completing the board when you run out of moves. You’ll quickly use up the watch an ad for 10 moves (since you can only do that a limited number of times per day) and at 1500, 3,000, and more coins to add moves, you’ll quickly go through however many coins you had accumulated. All this together has turned this game from being a fun distraction to being yet another money grab. There is no reason to have made the game so much harder and more frustrating other than trying to get more money from your players on top of the additional ad income you’re already getting. At the very least you should allow one ‘watch an ad for +10 moves per board regardless of how many times a player tries to complete a level” or, better yet, up the number of moves allowed to complete the puzzle (or get rid of the move limit altogether - maybe even at a one-time charge. Otherwise, this game is just going to be relegated to hiding in the shadows and slowly driving long time players away.

author: Feed the Frustrated
title: Would be 5 stars but they defeated themselves
content:
Too many ads and inefficient structure. I think this game has a great concept. I know that ads help keep games free but the ridiculous number of ads in this game make me think it is an advertising app that was developed as a gaming app. I guess you could say it's a good scam if they keep pushing all those ads maybe you'll pay... And this game even provides you with the experience of "add break" interruptions within your game for your dis-pleasure.  Also, process of the game itself is highly inefficient so paying to play isn't really an option in my opinion. I'll explain as concisely as I can why this game isn't worth the headache. 1. # moves: if this game deems that you can win it in 50 moves it will give you 51 moves. 2. # categories:  In combination with the limited moves is that there are more than four categories to be placed in the foundation slots.  Unlike Solitaire it's not just hearts, spades, diamonds, clubs. 3. The countdown that isn't a timer: EVERY MOVE COUNTS!! You don't get a timer, and you don't get lives. What you get is a countdown of moves. If you are dealt a hand where the cards cannot be categorized with each other or you run into a dead end-in solitaire what you normally do is go to your stockpile. In this game if you go to your stockpile it cost you a move. For every card you flip in the stockpile it will count down a move. If you find a card you can match and you move it from the stock pile to a stack it will count down a move. The same countdown continues for every move you make - matching stacks, using the stock pile, and moving from table to foundation slots. All matches; all movement cost you.
4. # moves vs # categories: The limited moves in combination with more than four categories makes it difficult to play the game efficiently. Not all word cards can be categorized where you might think. If you have the foundation categories WINTER, HOUSE AND DEVICES and you have the word card Heater and your place WINTER or HOUSE in a foundation slot that slot is now closed off until all the matches are made. However the word Heater is actually categorized under DEVICES. Your only option is to try and close out the foundation slot which costs you more moves before you can finally put DEVICES into a foundation slot and match it with the word Heater. 5. Blocking a stack: in this game you are allowed to place a foundation card onto a stack of matching cards. This would be like being able to put a king on top of a seven in solitaire. However this blocks the stack and if you find other cards to match you cannot add them-the stack has to be moved to a foundation slot in order for you to add any more matching cards. This basically blocks that slot while also causing you to countdown moves flipping past cards that you could've matched already. 6. No Rewards just Punishment... sorry I meant to say ads. As described above the moves countdown, when you're out of moves your options are to stop playing or watch an ad for five more moves. So you watch your ad, get your five moves, use three of them immediately on your stockpile, making a match or two, moving into a foundation pile and making another match. Then once again you are back to deciding if you want to keep playing or watch another ad for five more moves. You could restart and memorize as much as you can to try and win the game within the deemed count of moves, but then you're just playing the same game over and over… and don't worry you'll still get ads. As a matter of fact to add insult to injury this app will sell you extra moves through an ad and while you're trying to use those moves as efficiently as possible it'll stop you mid game and give you another ad to watch. 6.(continued) as mentioned above you get no real rewards. You can complete every single foundation stack and watch it disappear in a cheerful little chime but you get no additional lives you get no extra moves– all you get is more ads. I'll readily admit I only downloaded this game a couple of hours ago, and I don't understand why it has such high ratings– unless those ratings are bogus. There are some ratings that say they enjoy the game (I don't see how) but they also complain about the ads. I can't stand the process this game puts you through; this is why I say it is an advertising app that was develop as a gaming app.

author: AdsAdbuze
title: Tricks you to watch more ads
content:
This is a good game, but the excessive in-game advertising seriously damages the experience. Ads pop up repeatedly, almost like commercial breaks on television.

The game also feels deliberately designed to make players watch more ads. Whether you win or lose, the margin for error is extremely narrow. Even when you make what seems like a reasonable move, you can still lose a point. You only get around 10–20 chances to make mistakes, yet you barely have enough time to understand your deck and its mechanics.

So how are players realistically expected to win on their first attempt? The unforgiving point system makes failure almost inevitable, which then creates another opportunity to force players into watching two more ads.

The core game is good, but the aggressive and intrusive advertising system makes the experience feel more focused on generating ad revenue than allowing players to genuinely enjoy the game.

author: Cuquitina30
title: Stressing and expensive.
content:
I’ve been playing this game for a while now.   First I need to say that I don’t mind spending money on any game I like.  Developers work hard!  So, I got the ad free version, totally worth it. 
What makes this game not so fun for me, is that you have not enough moves at all.  This makes the game stressing and not relaxing or fun at all.  Flipping and moving a card take 2 moves from the number you have to work with, and honestly, losing because I didn’t have enough moves, added to getting stuck, makes this game not so much about skills or thinking, but more about money. 

The options to continue are insanely expensive.  You can spend ten bucks and get only enough game currency for only 2 times of continuing the game when you run out of moves. 

I really like the game, but I will end up deleting it because it’s taking me at least 5 or 6 times trying to pass a level if I don’t want to spend the money required to do so. 
Yes, you can watch ads.  But only for a very limited amount of times. 
Developers: don’t be greedy.  You don’t have to.
